newsitem.title: UK: Brent drifts on screen slide, all eyes on BP stems.
newsitem.headline: Brent drifts on screen slide, all eyes on BP stems.

text.p: North Sea physical crude languished in the doldrums on Thursday following a plunge in outright values with little immediate sign that improving refinery margins had yet injected fresh demand into an oversupplied market, traders said.

All eyes were on the fate of 12 unsold April BP cargoes overhanging the market, but a trader for the British major said the company's next step was not yet decided, noting arbitrage into the U.S. Gulf was not workable at the levels indicated by next week's CFDs.
Some players said they suspected the company was protecting a paper position ahead of sales of Brent into the United States.

Dated Brent was rumoured offered at May Brent -90 cents but few traders said they heard numbers mentioned in commercial discussion. The screen fall made many players hang back cautiously to see how low the numbers would go.
"The fall made the market twitchy," one commented.
Both Brent April 17-19 cargoes in Wednesday's chains were again kept by BP.
No dates were expected from the paper chains on Thursday.
Most crude differentials were still notionally assessed around Wednesday's levels, although some said Troll and regular Gullfaks A might be the exceptions and be offered weaker.
Paper was steady, with May Brent changing hands at $18.32, $18.35 and $18.38, some 80 cents weaker than Tuesday's values but in line with Wednesday's. April Brent changed hands at $17.63.
Outright Brent on the screen was easier. IPE May Brent futures were 17 cents weaker at $18.34 a barrel at 1247 GMT, catching up with a late sell-off in New York.
